objective: Remove duplicated Python planning precompilers through one native C implementation, retire the superseded toy evaluation runner with reproducible historical evidence, and preserve bounded planning behavior and useful test coverage.

requirements.native: The shared native manifest and staged precompiler preserves admitted graphs and all existing schema, cardinality, type, freshness, hash and accepted-result refusal boundaries.
requirements.coverage: Existing meaningful Python PTY, protocol and independent oracle coverage remains; the retired evaluation remains reproducible from the recorded baseline. No Python is hidden in shell or added to runtime.
requirements.sanitizer: The changed C precompiler passes the relevant behavior suite with address and undefined-behavior sanitizers.

selected_implementation: One shared C/JSON-C example precompiler; replace both internal entrypoints in place, preserve example payloads and independent checkers, retire old toy runner through exact Git-history replay.

rejected_alternatives.proposal: Shared Python module and thin wrappers
rejected_alternatives.reason: Keeps substantive planning logic in Python and retains two internal compatibility entrypoints without a published contract.

rejected_alternatives.proposal: Rewrite every Python test in C or shell
rejected_alternatives.reason: Unbounded rework and likely coverage loss; PTY and protocol drivers already use Python for a useful independent boundary.

verification: Original direct manifest/staged boundary cases with only entrypoint changes
Differential original/native graph comparison including empty/skipped/max manifests
Actual staged public workflow with exact acceptance and refusal controls
Inventory every tracked Python file plus embedded Python in shell; check no hiding or runtime addition
Independent sealed-source workflow acceptance and incorrect-artifact controls

measurement.estimates: uncalibrated ranges; unspecified costs remain unknown
measurement.causal_limit: One executed implementation cannot establish a semantic planning benefit; serial/parallel comparison isolates only fixed-graph scheduling.
